events.text: A blind swordswoman sits at the crossroads every morning and asks passers-by to throw a pebble at {him}. Nobody has hit {him} in eleven years. You hit {him} on the third try, and {he} laughs out loud.

effects.log: {npc} taps your wrist with {his} stick. 'You threw where I was going to be. That cannot be taught. Everything else can.' {He} teaches you for years, at the crossroads, with pebbles.
{He} is still laughing when you are out of earshot.

events.text: {npc} is very old now and sends for you. {He} gives you {his} sword, which has never had a name, and asks you to throw one last pebble.

effects.log: {He} catches it without moving, smiles, and says your form has finally become yours. {He} dies that winter, at the crossroads, in the sun.
You sit until evening. {He} tells you everything {he} never told you about the sword, which turns out to be about you.

events.text: A monk expelled from Shaolin for drinking wins a bet against you, a whole jar of wine, by standing on one finger for an hour. {He} offers to teach you, if you keep the jars coming.

effects.log: {npc} is drunk every afternoon and terrifying every morning. {His} palm method is the real Shaolin one, with the wine added in.
The abbot sighs. '{He} is still the best of us,' {he} says. 'Do not tell {him} I said so.'

events.text: {npc} has stopped drinking. That is how you know it is serious. {He} asks you to carry {him} to the temple gate {he} was thrown out of, decades ago.

effects.log: The abbot meets you at the gate and bows to {him}. {He} dies inside the walls, forgiven, with a jar of wine you smuggled in under your robe.
effects.npcDie: old age, inside the temple walls

choices.text: Ask {him} for the last lesson first

effects.log: 'Drink less than I did,' {he} says, 'and fight more than I did.' Then {he} walks up the steps alone.

events.text: A ragged old man is teaching village boys to march with sticks. {He} moves like an army. {He} was one: the general the court exiled for winning a war the wrong way.

ok.log: {npc} teaches you the spear, the formation and the long patience of a siege. 'One person is a small army,' {he} says. 'Train like one.'

fail.log: {He} watches you stumble through the first drill, shakes {his} head, and goes back to the boys. The offer is not repeated.

choices.text: Join the stick-drill with the boys

effects.log: It is surprisingly hard work. The old man nods at you once, which the boys tell you is a great honour.

events.text: A pardon arrives for {npc} from the new Emperor, years too late. {He} reads it twice and hands it to you.

effects.log: {He} walks into the throne room in {his} old armour, bows exactly as low as {he} must, and walks out again. On the road home {he} laughs the whole way.
'I did not need their word,' {he} says, 'only yours.' {He} teaches you {his} last formation by the fire.

events.arc: The Herb Woman of the Mountain
events.text: You are dying of a snake bite in the mountains when an old woman finds you, cuts the wound, sucks the poison, and slaps you for being stupid. {His} hut smells of a hundred herbs.

effects.log: {npc} teaches medicine first, poison second and the martial arts third, which {he} says is the right order. {He} is right.
{He} gives you a pouch of herbs and tells you not to come back stupid.

events.arc: The Herb Woman of the Mountain
events.text: {npc} asks you to find a herb that grows only where a tribulation struck. {He} does not say what it is for. You suspect it is for {him}.

ok.log: It gives {him} two more years. {He} spends them teaching you the last of {his} art, the part {he} said {he} would never teach anyone.

fail.log: The herb is not where the maps say. You come back with mud to the knees, and {he} says it was a long shot, and teaches you a little regardless.

effects.log: 'For you,' {he} says. 'A pill for the day you face your own tribulation.' {He} brews it, and you keep it.

events.text: The quiet man who sells tofu at the end of your street catches a falling roof tile behind {his} back without turning around. Then {he} looks at you, because you saw.

ok.log: {npc} teaches you, at night, everything a retired assassin knows about not being where the blade lands. {He} never teaches you how to kill. You learn it anyway.

fail.log: The promise rings hollow, and {he} hears it. The tofu is not sold to you for a month, and the secret stays between you.

effects.log: {He} nods slowly. The tofu is very good. You never mention it.

events.text: {npc}'s past arrives at the tofu shop: three blades from the guild {he} left. {He} asks you to go home. You do not go home.

ok.log: Two of them leave. One stays, buried behind the shop. Your master sells tofu for another ten years.

fail.deathCause: an assassin guild's blades at a tofu shop
fail.log: Two of the three blades are better than you. Your master finishes the work, and you carry the wounds.

ok.log: A great deal of silver and a promise. The guild takes both and leaves. Your master never asks what it cost.

fail.log: The guild takes your offer as an insult and your master's name as the price. You leave with a broken rib and a deadline.

mem.note: ran for the watch when the blades came

effects.log: By the time you come back with the watch, it is over. One blade lies behind the shop; the other two are gone. {npc} is cutting tofu with a bandaged hand and does not look up.

events.arc: The Scholar of the Empty Hall
events.text: A failed scholar who never passed the exams runs a school with no students. {He} insists the martial arts are a branch of the classics, and proves it by disarming a thief with a calligraphy brush.

effects.log: {npc} teaches you the classics and the brush and, somewhere in between, a sword method written as poetry. You read it for years before you realise you are fighting.

choices.text: Ask {him} to teach you to read instead

effects.log: {He} is delighted. You read a great deal. The sword in the poems waits for someone else.

events.arc: The Scholar of the Empty Hall
events.text: {npc} is going blind and asks you to read {him} {his} own commentary on the classics, all forty volumes, before {he} forgets what {he} wrote.

effects.log: It takes a winter. In the thirty-eighth volume you find the sword method, complete, hidden in the commentary. {He} smiles when you stop reading.
The academy that failed {him} puts {his} name in the library. {He} cannot see it. You describe it to {him} every day.

events.text: The old ferrywoman poles {his} boat across the river with {his} eyes closed, and when bandits try to board {him}, they all somehow end up in the water. {He} does not stop poling.

effects.log: {npc} takes your coin and teaches you to stand in a boat. That takes a year. Then {he} teaches you the rest, which takes many more.
{He} winks at you at the far bank.

events.text: The river is flooding and {npc} will not leave {his} boat, because people on the far bank are trapped and no one else will go.

ok.npcPass: old age, a year after the great flood
ok.log: Twenty-three crossings in a night. {He} dies a year later, in {his} sleep, and the whole river town carries {his} boat to the grave.

fail.deathCause: a flood, in an old woman's boat
fail.log: The current is stronger than either of you. {He} gets you both across, barely, and the far bank is emptier than you hoped.

choices.text: Take the pole from {him} and go alone

ok.log: {He} shouts instructions from the bank all night. In the morning {he} says you are ready, and gives you the boat.

fail.deathCause: a flood, alone in a ferry
fail.log: The pole is too long and the river too wide. {He} shouts from the bank, then takes it back and crosses anyway.

choices.text: Keep a signal fire burning on the bank

effects.log: All night you feed a fire on the bank so {npc} can find the landing in the dark. {He} makes eleven crossings alone. In the morning {he} is grey with cold and says nothing about the fire, which from {him} is thanks.

events.arc: The Hermit of the Cold Peak
events.text: You climb the Cold Peak on a dare and find a hermit who has not spoken in twenty years. {He} breaks {his} silence to tell you that you are holding your breath wrong.

ok.log: {npc} speaks again, a little, and only about breathing. Your qi doubles in a year. {He} says that is the least of it.

fail.log: The breath will not come as {he} wants it. {He} says nothing, and you climb down with a headache and a blush.

effects.log: You breathe differently the whole way down, without meaning to.

events.arc: The Hermit of the Cold Peak
events.text: {npc} says {he} will go into {his} final seclusion and not come out. {He} asks you to seal the cave behind {him}, and to come back in a hundred years.

effects.log: {He} gives you the last breath of {his} method through the closing gap. You come back every year anyway, and talk to the stone.

choices.text: Ask {him} to stay a little longer

effects.log: {He} stays a year, and talks more in that year than in the twenty before it. Then {he} seals the cave with {his} own hands.
